# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47 (Bi-Vb Pc47)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc47  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47  
**Title (English, from literature):** Not relinquishing a communal robe  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47 (*Āvasathacīvara*) is a gender-specific disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the use of a communal menstrual robe (*āvasathacīvara*, literally "communal dwelling robe" or "household cloth") [Hüsken 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun who uses the communal robe for two or three nights and washes it on the fourth day must relinquish it to another nun, a probationer (*sikkhamānā*), or a novice (*sāmaṇerī*); continuing to wear it beyond the intended period without giving it up constitutes an expiable offense (*pācittiya*) [Hirakawa 1982; Hüsken 1997; Collett 2014]. Modern scholars observe that while the garment functioned as a hygienic aid, its institutionalization and sharing protocols also prevented individual possessiveness of communal property and conformed to broader ancient Indian and Brahmanical social norms regarding menstrual conduct and seclusion [Sarao and Long 2017; Hüsken 1997; Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth].

Full parallels are preserved in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Bi-Pm Pc 47) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*, as well as across the Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya traditions in Chinese and Tibetan translations (such as the Mūlasarvāstivāda *rajaścoda* or *sme gab* rules) [Collett 2014; Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth]. English translations of the rule have been made by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth].
